key_insight: Even under very strong adverse-pressure gradients, the outer region of turbulent boundary layers shows component-wise self-similarity when each mean-defect or Reynolds-stress profile is normalized by its value at a common outer location.
engineering_relevance: This provides compact reference profiles for assessing turbulence models and reconstructing APG boundary-layer statistics without needing a single universal scaling law.
method: Compiled a benchmark from new DNS of a suction--blowing separation bubble plus published APG/TBL data.
Covered a wide range of Clauser parameters and Reynolds numbers, then normalized six quantities by their value at a chosen outer reference height $y_s$ (shown with $y_s=0.5\delta$).
Tested collapse across two mean-velocity defects and four Reynolds-stress components and quantified outer self-similarity via collapse-error analysis.
evidence_signal: The benchmark spans $\beta_e=0.04$--$180$ and $Re_\theta=530$--$19000$, and the abstract reports consistent outer-shape collapse for all six quantities, with velocity defects collapsing for $y/\delta\gtrsim0.2$ and stresses for $y/\delta\gtrsim0.4$.
watch_item: The observed similarity is component-wise and depends on choosing an outer-region reference location, so it should not be interpreted as a universal single-scaling collapse for the entire boundary layer.
paper_title: Component-wise outer similarity of turbulent boundary layers with strong adverse-pressure gradient
